game: LV @ WAS | 2025-09-21 13:00 ET | WAS -2.5 | total 43.5 | outdoor, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Closing line has Washington -2.5 in a 43.5-point outdoor game, implied WAS 23.0 / LV 20.5, so the market expects a one-score, full-snap game even with Jayden Daniels already Out. Daniels was the Commanders' leading rusher (15 carries, 88 yards over weeks 1-2) and Las Vegas has allowed only 3.40 YPC with 3 runs of 10+, so the path to 23 points is not a QB-run or explosive-run script. Base flow is Washington in a short/intermediate pass game to Deebo Samuel (18 targets, 121 yards, 85 air) and Zach Ertz (13/90/87), with a committee of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (14/99) and Austin Ekeler (14/43) replacing some but not all of the lost QB carries. Las Vegas stays competitive behind Jakobi Meyers (22 targets, 165 yards) and Brock Bowers (16/141) because Washington blitzes 32% and LV's EPA/db is +0.43 versus the blitz against -0.34 with no blitz. Ashton Jeanty (30 carries, 81 yards, 2.7 YPC) keeps the lead-back role but is not in a clock-killing script.
script.flip1: Washington gets up by two scores anyway, Croskey-Merritt and Ekeler grind the clock, and LV abandons Jeanty. Meyers, Bowers and Donte Thornton (8 targets, 205 air yards) see pass volume spike while Samuel's yardage stalls and Jeanty's rush line dies.
script.flip2: The unnamed backup wilts against LV's 28% blitz — Washington was already -0.19 EPA/db versus the blitz with Daniels and -0.02 without it — LV leads, Washington has to throw vertically (Terry McLaurin already has 187 air yards on only 75 yards), and Jeanty's carries rise late. Unsaved outdoor weather is the other flip into a sub-43.5 slog.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse injury report: Jayden Daniels Out (knee), Noah Brown Out (groin), John Bates Out (groin), LV CB Decamerion Richardson Questionable (hamstring). Daniels's 15 carries/88 rush yards leave the WAS run game; they do not automatically transfer because scramble yards are not designed handoffs, and the remaining carries are already split evenly (Croskey-Merritt 14/99, Ekeler 14/43, Jeremy McNichols 4/25). Brown's 7 targets/36 yards/96 air yards leave the WR room. That air-yard profile (about 13.7 aDOT) looks more like McLaurin (13 targets, 187 air, 75 yards) or Jaylin Lane (6/13/36) than Samuel (85 air on 18 targets), so Samuel is not the automatic heir — he gains only if the new QB funnels the quick game to the existing target leader. Bates has no target line in the pack, so his absence is a blocking loss, not a Zach Ertz target bump. Richardson is Questionable, not Out, and no coverage chart says who he would have covered; do not treat a WAS WR as facing a confirmed backup. No WAS defensive back is Out, so no LV pass-catcher has a sleeper-defender bump. Final inactives (~90 minutes pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.overlap: Samuel's usage is short (85 air yards on 18 targets, 4.7 aDOT) into the only LV hole that is extreme, middle 9.71 YPA, though that split is only 14 throws. Meyers is the LV target leader (22 targets, 182 air) into a WAS defense that bleeds outside (right 7.6, left 6.79) and blitzes at the rate LV has destroyed. McLaurin-to-outside is a weaker overlap because deep efficiency has already failed (75 yards on 187 air) and the new QB plus a 28% LV blitz cuts against explosives. Jeanty-to-WAS-run is a soft overlap (4.14 YPC allowed versus his own 2.7) but not a clean over.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Samuel stopped at 44 again because the middle 9.71 was 14 throws of noise, Ertz and Ekeler took the quick game, and the backup never sustained drives against a 28% blitz that already had Washington at -0.19 EPA/db. Brown's 96 air yards went to McLaurin or Lane, not Deebo, so the sleeper story was the wrong player. Meyers stopped at 68 because Washington blitzed less than 32% once it had a lead, LV's +0.43 versus-blitz EPA was a two-game spike with no play count behind it, and a one-score dog spread never forced extra pass volume. Jeanty and the clock, or a weather slog that was never forecast in the pack, finished both lines under.
slip_story: One competitive-game pass story, not a grind and not a TD slip: WAS replaces Daniels's 88 rush yards with short throws to Samuel because LV's run defense is the strong side of the ball, and LV's Meyers exploits the 32% blitz in a 20.5-implied, non-blowout script. The two legs win together if both offenses stay on the field. They lose together if the game becomes a weather slog or a WAS clock-kill. No third leg: Croskey-Merritt under 49.5 dies if the favorite grinds, Jeanty over 40.5 is form-stuck at 38 and 43, Bowers 103/38 is too wild against a 4.2 middle, and McLaurin is a conflicting deep-ball read with the new QB. Max two, no receptions, no passing yards, no TDs.
